-- The five windows' shared slot count cap: the backpack is always exactly 16 -- (GetContainerNumSlots(0) never varies — PACK_SLOTS is a wire constant); the -- equipped-bag windows show up to this many (5 rows × 4 columns — the reference template's -- true max is 36, but 20 is vanilla's largest actual equippable bag, and building out to 36 -- slot buttons per window for content that can never exist would be pure waste. Hides the -- unused tail via BenillaBagSlot_Update's physIndex-past-size branch, same as the backpack. BENILLA_BAG_WINDOW_MAX_SLOTS = 20
-- The keyring's container id (ref MainMenuBarBagButtons.lua:1) — decision 0765. It is an -- ordinary container in every respect the seam cares about: the app feeds it like any other -- bag (its slots are the player descriptor's own 81.., no container object), and every -- container verb, the cursor, the pending-op lock and the wire drains take it unchanged. -- What makes it special is only what the reference makes special: the window's art, its -- open/close sound, and the fact that its capacity is not a wire field. KEYRING_CONTAINER = -2
-- The keyring's usable slot count (ref GetKeyRingSize, ContainerFrame.lua:773). The -- reference recomputes a level ladder in Lua (4 / 8 at 40 / 12 at 50 / 16 above 60) that the -- server enforces identically (Player::GetMaxKeyringSize); benilla computes it once app-side -- and feeds it as the container's own size, so this reads it back rather than keeping a -- second copy of the ladder that could drift from the one the feed uses. function GetKeyRingSize() return GetContainerNumSlots(KEYRING_CONTAINER) end
-- BenillaBagSlot_OnLoad(button, physIndex): physIndex is the button's CHAIN position (1 = -- bottom-right, growing up-and-left — the anchor order below), not the game slot. The ref's -- own formula (index = size - j + 1, ContainerFrame.lua:426/446) maps chain position → game -- slot dynamically in BenillaBagSlot_Update, so slot 1 always reads top-left regardless of -- how many of the window's slots are actually occupied — recomputed every Update (the ref -- only computes it once, at window generation; recomputing is a strict robustness win for -- the rare live bag-swap case, not a behavior change for a size that never moves). function BenillaBagSlot_OnLoad(button, physIndex) button.physIndex = physIndex button.icon = getglobal(button:GetName() .. "Icon") button.count = getglobal(button:GetName() .. "Count") -- Both buttons must reach OnClick (the default set is LeftButtonUp only): LEFT-click is the -- pickup gesture (PickupContainerItem — pick up / place / swap on the cursor); RIGHT-click -- cancels a held cursor, else uses the slot (the C side sells it when a merchant is open — -- our container drain forks). button:RegisterForClicks("LeftButtonUp", "RightButtonUp") -- The drag trio (decision 0216 §3): click-carry and drag are ONE code path in the -- reference (ContainerFrame.xml:40-55 routes OnDragStart/OnReceiveDrag to the same -- OnClick("LeftButton", ignoreModifiers=1) the plain click uses) — see -- BenillaBagSlot_OnClick below for the identical routing (its own `ignoreModifiers` -- suppresses the shift-split fork, the reference's own contract for drag/receive). button:RegisterForDrag("LeftButton") BenillaBagSlot_Update(button) end
function BenillaBagSlot_OnClick(button, mouseButton, ignoreModifiers) if button.slot == nil then return end -- a hidden button (physIndex past the bag's size) local bagId = button:GetParent():GetID() if mouseButton == "LeftButton" then -- The reference's own five returns (ContainerFrame.lua:241) — decision 1199 -- put this binding back on its 1.12 shape. local texture, itemCount, locked, quality, readable = GetContainerItemInfo(bagId, button.slot) -- The modifier fork, the reference's own order (ContainerFrame.lua:563-579; -- BankFrame.lua:141-152 for a bank slot, which is this same handler at container -- -1). `ignoreModifiers` (the drag-trio calls, both true) suppresses it whole — -- the reference's drag/receive contract. -- -- CTRL: preview the item on your own character in the dressing room (decision 1060). if IsControlKeyDown() and not ignoreModifiers then DressUpItemLink(GetContainerItemLink(bagId, button.slot)) return end -- SHIFT: post the item's link into the chat edit box if it's open, ELSE split the -- stack. The ref's own `else` (l.567-577) — and note it gates on `IsShown()` here -- where its siblings use `IsVisible()`; ours are the same thing (the edit box's only -- parent is UIParent), so the ref's own word is quoted at each site. if IsShiftKeyDown() and not ignoreModifiers then -- The visibility test is the REF'S fork, not the helper's: with chat open this -- arm never splits, even in the one benilla state where nothing can be posted -- (an unresolved template — `BenillaChatEdit_InsertLink`'s own note). if ChatFrameEditBox and ChatFrameEditBox:IsShown() then BenillaChatEdit_InsertLink(GetContainerItemLink(bagId, button.slot)) return end if texture ~= nil and not locked and (itemCount or 1) >= 2 then button.SplitStack = function(btn, n) SplitContainerItem(bagId, btn.slot, n) BenillaBagWindow_Repaint(btn:GetParent()) end -- Ref ContainerFrameItemButton_OnLoad/_OnClick (ContainerFrame.lua:558-560, -- 573-576): the owner's own SplitStack closure carries the bag/slot so -- StackSplitFrameOkay_Click's generic `owner.SplitStack(owner, split)` call -- needs no window-specific knowledge. SplitContainerItem lives in cursor.rs -- rather than container.rs — it is the one container-named verb whose -- payload is the cursor's, not a bag's — but like every container verb it is -- a plain top-level global (decision 1198). OpenStackSplitFrame(itemCount, button, "BOTTOMRIGHT", "TOPRIGHT") end return end -- A plain click hides any open split frame (ref ContainerFrame.lua:581) before the -- ordinary pickup/place proceeds. local split = getglobal("StackSplitFrame") if split then split:Hide() end -- PickupContainerItem is the single drag entry point (real client): an empty cursor -- picks this slot up; a held cursor places/swaps into it (same slot = cancel). Hide the -- hover tooltip (the item just left the slot for the cursor) and repaint so the picked -- slot dims / un-dims immediately — the swap itself settles when the server answers. PickupContainerItem(bagId, button.slot) GameTooltip:Hide() BenillaBagWindow_Repaint(button:GetParent()) elseif mouseButton == "RightButton" then -- A held cursor cancels (client-side, nothing sent); otherwise use/equip/sell the slot. if CursorHasItem() then ClearCursor() BenillaBagWindow_Repaint(button:GetParent()) else UseContainerItem(bagId, button.slot) end end end
-- Hover: the era-true GameTooltip:SetBagItem(bag, slot) — the ENGINE renders the full -- item tooltip from the template store and owns the sell-price money law (real instance -- + merchant open + repair off ⇒ OnTooltipAddMoney(SellPrice × stack), or the -- ITEM_UNSELLABLE line — wow-re ui/scratch/tooltip-money.md's byte-verified gate, -- decision 0274 P1). The durability-adjusted damaged price is deferred until durability -- damage reaches the feed (a pristine item reduces to SellPrice × stack, the case we -- ship). Nothing shows while the template is in flight — the OnUpdate re-enter fills it. function BenillaBagSlot_OnEnter(button) if button.slot == nil then return end local bagId = button:GetParent():GetID() local texture, itemCount, locked, quality, readable = GetContainerItemInfo(bagId, button.slot) -- An emptied slot drops its tooltip (ref ContainerFrame_Update's texture-nil branch, -- ContainerFrame.lua:281-283) — without this the OnUpdate re-enter below would leave -- a stale tooltip up after the item is sold or moved out from under the hover. if not texture then if GameTooltip:IsOwned(button) then GameTooltip:Hide() end return end -- Ref ContainerFrameItemButton_OnEnter (ContainerFrame.lua:602-612) verbatim: a slot -- in the RIGHT half of the screen hangs its tooltip LEFT, so it never runs off the -- edge (the bag lives at the bottom-right — this is the ref's own screen-edge answer, -- a side-pick, not a clamp). if (button:GetRight() or 0) >= (GetScreenWidth() / 2) then GameTooltip:SetOwner(button, "ANCHOR_LEFT") else GameTooltip:SetOwner(button, "ANCHOR_RIGHT") end GameTooltip:SetBagItem(bagId, button.slot) -- The pouch/magnifier cursor (ref ContainerFrameItemButton_OnEnter tail, -- ContainerFrame.lua l.636-642): merchant open on the MERCHANT tab and not repair -- mode → the sell cursor over this slot; else a readable item (a mail letter copy — -- right-click opens the reader) → the Inspect magnifier; anything else restores the -- base cursor. The OnUpdate re-enter keeps it current while hovering (the ref's own -- loop). The ref's `IsControlKeyDown() and hasItem` magnifier arm (l.638) is the -- dress-up preview's own cursor tell — it landed with the dressing room (decision -- 1060); `info` is non-nil above, which is the ref's `hasItem`. if MerchantFrame and MerchantFrame:IsShown() and MerchantFrame.selectedTab == 1 and not InRepairMode() then ShowContainerSellCursor(bagId, button.slot) elseif readable or IsControlKeyDown() then ShowInspectCursor() else ResetCursor() end GameTooltip:Show() end
function BenillaBagSlot_OnLeave(button) GameTooltip:Hide() -- Ref ItemButton OnLeave (ContainerFrame.xml): the hover's sell cursor drops with it. ResetCursor() end
-- Ref ContainerFrameItemButton_OnUpdate (ContainerFrame.lua:645-660): while the tooltip -- is ours, re-run OnEnter every frame — the ref ships this loop UNTHROTTLED (its -- updateTooltip throttle is commented out in 1.12). It is the real client's own refresh -- mechanism: a tooltip set while the item template was still in flight fills itself in -- the moment the answer lands, no re-hover. function BenillaBagSlot_OnUpdate(button) if GameTooltip:IsOwned(button) then BenillaBagSlot_OnEnter(button) end end
-- The item's use-cooldown sweep (ref ContainerFrame_UpdateCooldown, -- ContainerFrame.lua:295-299, verbatim shape over our container dialect). function BenillaBagSlot_UpdateCooldown(button, bagId) local cooldown = getglobal(button:GetName() .. "Cooldown") local start, duration, enable = GetContainerItemCooldown(bagId, button.slot) CooldownFrame_SetTimer(cooldown, start, duration, enable) end
-- The physIndex → game-slot resolution (the module doc above) + the paint (ref -- ContainerFrame_Update, ContainerFrame.lua:234-293). Shared by every window's slot -- buttons. The occupied/empty fork drives the cooldown exactly as the ref does -- (l.248-253: occupied → UpdateCooldown, empty → Cooldown:Hide()). function BenillaBagSlot_Update(button) local bagId = button:GetParent():GetID() local size = GetContainerNumSlots(bagId) if button.physIndex > size then button.slot = nil button:Hide() return end button.slot = size - button.physIndex + 1 button:Show() local texture, itemCount, locked = GetContainerItemInfo(bagId, button.slot) if texture ~= nil or itemCount ~= nil then BenillaBagSlot_UpdateCooldown(button, bagId) button.icon:SetTexture(texture or BENILLA_FALLBACK_ICON) -- A locked slot (its item is up on the cursor, or a send is still pending -- server-side, decision 0216 §4/0218 §3) dims, the real client's drag feedback. if locked then button.icon:SetVertexColor(0.4, 0.4, 0.4) else button.icon:SetVertexColor(1, 1, 1) end if (itemCount or 1) > 1 then button.count:SetText(itemCount) else button.count:SetText("") end else button.icon:SetTexture(nil) button.count:SetText("") getglobal(button:GetName() .. "Cooldown"):Hide() end end
-- The generic per-window repaint (decision 0216 slice 2): every slot up to this window's -- cap, the title (GetBagName — dynamic since a live bag swap changes it), and the money -- purse (backpack only, ContainerFrame.lua l.314). BenillaBagFrame_Update (below) is the -- backpack's zero-arg convenience alias, kept for existing callers (UiPanels.xml's -- OpenBackpack/CloseBackpack, and the tests that patch it directly). function BenillaBagWindow_Update(frame) local bagId = frame:GetID() local maxSlots = (bagId == 0) and 16 or BENILLA_BAG_WINDOW_MAX_SLOTS -- The backpack predates the $parent-prefixed slot naming (BenillaBagSlot1..16, not -- BenillaBagFrameSlot1..16 — its buttons are hand-authored, not $parent-templated) and -- several existing tests reference that exact name directly; every other window's slots -- DO follow frame:GetName().."Slot"..i (the virtual template's $parentSlotN). local slotPrefix = (bagId == 0) and "BenillaBagSlot" or (frame:GetName() .. "Slot") for i = 1, maxSlots do local button = getglobal(slotPrefix .. i) if button then BenillaBagSlot_Update(button) end end local title = getglobal(frame:GetName() .. "Name") if title then -- The keyring is titled from the localized KEYRING string, not GetBagName — it has -- no bag ITEM to be named after (ref ContainerFrame.lua l.418). if bagId == KEYRING_CONTAINER then title:SetText(KEYRING) else title:SetText(GetBagName(bagId) or "") end end if bagId == 0 then BenillaMoney_Set("BenillaBagMoney", GetMoney()) elseif bagId == KEYRING_CONTAINER then -- Fixed art, again because there is no bag item: the keyring's own portrait -- (ref ContainerFrame.lua l.419) and its own background variant, snug-fitted to the -- level-gated slot count exactly like an equipped bag. -- The GLOBAL form, which is the reference's own (ContainerFrame.lua l.419 -- writes exactly this call) — 1.12 has no such Texture method. SetPortraitToTexture(frame:GetName() .. "Portrait", "Interface\\ContainerFrame\\KeyRing-Bag-Icon") local size = GetContainerNumSlots(bagId) if size > 0 then BenillaBagWindow_FitBackground(frame, size) end else -- The window's portrait is the bag's OWN item icon (the real client's -- C-side SetBagPortaitTexture), not the default backpack art. An equipped bag -- (1..4) reads its doll slot (19+bagId, Bag0Slot..Bag3Slot); a bank bag (5..10, -- decision 0604) reads the app-resolved bank-bag feed instead — the doll array -- stops at the equipped bags, so GetInventoryItemTexture can't reach the vault's. -- Falls back to the backpack icon while the item template's icon is in flight. local portrait = getglobal(frame:GetName() .. "Portrait") if portrait then local icon if bagId >= 5 then icon = BenillaGetBankBagTexture(bagId - 4) else icon = GetInventoryItemTexture("player", 19 + bagId) end if icon then -- The circular crop (the real SetBagPortaitTexture is C-side and masks the -- icon to the ring's inscribed circle): a raw square icon pokes its corners -- past the round rim — the director's bank-bag popout artifact. SetPortraitToTexture(frame:GetName() .. "Portrait", icon) else -- The backpack fallback art is authored round — no crop to apply. portrait:SetTexture("Interface\\Buttons\\Button-Backpack-Up") end end -- Equipped bags snug-fit their stitched background to the live row count. local size = GetContainerNumSlots(bagId) if size > 0 then BenillaBagWindow_FitBackground(frame, size) end end end
-- Fit an equipped-bag window's stitched background (BgTop/BgMiddle/BgBottom, authored in the -- template above) and its OWN height to the bag's actual row count. This is a transcription of -- the real client's ContainerFrame_GenerateFrame (the id~=0 branch) as shipped in the 1.12.1 -- MPQ (Interface\FrameXML\ContainerFrame.lua) — every constant below is the reference's, not a -- measured approximation. rows = ceil(size/4). The TOP piece carries the header + the first -- well row; the MIDDLE tiles the remaining rows; the BOTTOM is the frame's bottom rim. The -- slot buttons anchor UP from the frame's BOTTOMRIGHT (first at -12,9) and hide past `size` -- (BenillaBagSlot_Update), so nothing here touches them — only the art + the frame height. -- Which UI-Bag-Components variant a window is stitched from — the ref's own `bagTextureSuffix` -- (ContainerFrame_GenerateFrame, ContainerFrame.lua l.326-334): the bank bags get the -- tinted "-Bank" plate, the keyring the "-Keyring" one, an equipped bag the plain sheet. -- All three atlases are 256x512 with the same band layout, so FitBackground's tex-coords -- are shared verbatim and only the file differs. (Ours ALSO applies the "-Bank" arm, which -- benilla had been quietly skipping — the bank popouts have been drawing ordinary bag art -- since decision 0604.) function BenillaBagWindow_BgTexture(bagId) local suffix = "" if bagId >= 5 then suffix = "-Bank" elseif bagId == KEYRING_CONTAINER then suffix = "-Keyring" end return "Interface\\ContainerFrame\\UI-Bag-Components" .. suffix end
function BenillaBagWindow_FitBackground(frame, size) local name = frame:GetName() local top = getglobal(name .. "BgTop") local middle = getglobal(name .. "BgMiddle") local bottom = getglobal(name .. "BgBottom") if not (top and middle and bottom) then return end -- Re-set every fit, as the ref does at every generate: the template authors the plain -- sheet, and a window's kind is only known from its id. local bg = BenillaBagWindow_BgTexture(frame:GetID()) top:SetTexture(bg) middle:SetTexture(bg) bottom:SetTexture(bg) local rowH = 41 -- rowHeight local rows = math.ceil(size / 4) if rows < 1 then rows = 1 end -- isPlusTwoBag: a size leaving a remainder of 2 (6/10/14/18) has a 2-well top row, and the -- texture carries a whole separate top band for it. local plusTwo = (size - math.floor(size / 4) * 4) == 2 local topH if plusTwo then topH = 72 top:SetTexCoord(0, 1, 0.189453125, 0.330078125) elseif rows == 1 then topH = 86 -- one row only: chop the bottom of the texture top:SetTexCoord(0, 1, 0.00390625, 0.16796875) else topH = 94 top:SetTexCoord(0, 1, 0.00390625, 0.18359375) end top:SetHeight(topH) -- The top piece already carries one row, so the middle tiles `rows - 1` more. Its height is -- one row short of a clean multiple: the reference's firstRowPixelOffset = 9 accounts for -- the 9px the BOTTOM rim itself contributes to the final row's frame. Getting this wrong -- pushes the rim a row-fraction too low and bleeds the NEXT row's wells in above it. local middleH = 0 bottom:ClearAllPoints() if rows > 1 then -- A single middle piece spans at most ROWS_IN_BG_TEXTURE (6) rows; the reference -- cycles up to MAX_BG_TEXTURES for windows taller than that. Our largest window is a -- 20-slot bag (4 middle rows) and the keyring caps at 16 (3), so one always suffices. middleH = (rows - 1) * rowH - 9 middle:SetHeight(middleH) middle:SetTexCoord(0, 1, 0.353515625, middleH / 512 + 0.353515625) middle:Show() bottom:SetPoint("TOPRIGHT", middle, "BOTTOMRIGHT", 0, 0) else -- One row: the rim seats straight under the top piece. (The reference anchors it to the -- hidden middle's TOP, which is the same point — the middle hangs off the top's bottom.) middle:Hide() bottom:SetPoint("TOPRIGHT", top, "BOTTOMRIGHT", 0, 0) end -- The bottom rim is a FIXED 10px band at texture v 0.330078125..0.349609375 — the strip -- immediately below the plus-two top band, and the only true outer bottom border in the -- texture. The reference never rescales or re-coords it; it is authored once in XML. local bottomH = 10 bottom:SetHeight(bottomH) bottom:SetTexCoord(0, 1, 0.330078125, 0.349609375) frame:SetHeight(topH + middleH + bottomH) -- A live size change (a bag swap while the stack is open) shifts every window stacked above -- this one; re-run the stack layout so they re-seat against the new height. if frame:IsShown() then BenillaBagStack_Relayout() end end
function BenillaBagFrame_Update() BenillaBagWindow_Update(BenillaBagFrame) end
-- Routes a repaint through the backpack's own zero-arg BenillaBagFrame_Update alias when -- `frame` IS the backpack — preserving that global's observability (existing tests patch it -- directly to count backpack repaints, e.g. delete_item_tests.rs's stuck-darkening -- regression check) — and BenillaBagWindow_Update generically for every other window. Every -- runtime repaint trigger (a slot click, an event, OpenAllBags' pre-show paint) goes -- through this (BenillaBagBarSlot_OnClick reaches it through the ToggleBag global too). function BenillaBagWindow_Repaint(frame) if frame:GetID() == 0 then BenillaBagFrame_Update() else BenillaBagWindow_Update(frame) end end
-- OnLoad/OnEvent (generic, shared by all five windows — each already receives `frame`, so -- deriving bagId from `frame:GetID()` needs no per-window body). function BenillaBagFrame_OnLoad(frame) frame:RegisterEvent("BAG_UPDATE") -- The engine fires ITEM_LOCK_CHANGED(bag, slot) on every cursor pickup/clear AND every -- pending-op send/resolve (decisions 0216 §4/0218 §3) — including clears the bag never -- clicked through (the delete popup's No, ESC; a server failure), which the click-time -- repaint can't see. The reference ContainerFrame repaints on exactly this event. frame:RegisterEvent("ITEM_LOCK_CHANGED") -- Item cooldown starts/ends (ref ContainerFrame_OnLoad, ContainerFrame.lua:21 — -- BAG_UPDATE_COOLDOWN carries no bag argument; every open window refreshes). frame:RegisterEvent("BAG_UPDATE_COOLDOWN") -- The real backpack MoneyFrame refreshes on PLAYER_MONEY (SmallMoneyFrame's own OnEvent); -- keep the purse live while the window is open. Backpack only — the other windows never -- show a purse, so there's nothing for them to refresh. if frame:GetID() == 0 then frame:RegisterEvent("PLAYER_MONEY") end end
function BenillaBagFrame_OnEvent(frame) if event == "PLAYER_MONEY" then BenillaMoney_Set("BenillaBagMoney", GetMoney()) return end -- The cooldown-only refresh (ref ContainerFrame_UpdateCooldowns via OnEvent, -- ContainerFrame.lua:243-253's loop shape): no bag argument — sweep every shown -- slot of THIS window, no full repaint. if event == "BAG_UPDATE_COOLDOWN" then local bagId = frame:GetID() local maxSlots = (bagId == 0) and 16 or BENILLA_BAG_WINDOW_MAX_SLOTS local slotPrefix = (bagId == 0) and "BenillaBagSlot" or (frame:GetName() .. "Slot") for i = 1, maxSlots do local button = getglobal(slotPrefix .. i) if button and button.slot then BenillaBagSlot_UpdateCooldown(button, bagId) end end return end -- BAG_UPDATE / ITEM_LOCK_CHANGED name their bag in arg1; only THIS window's own bag -- repaints (ref ContainerFrame_OnEvent, ContainerFrame.lua:26-44: `this:GetID() == arg1`). if (event == "BAG_UPDATE" or event == "ITEM_LOCK_CHANGED") and arg1 ~= frame:GetID() then return end BenillaBagWindow_Repaint(frame) end
-- ToggleBag / ToggleBackpack / OpenAllBags (ref ContainerFrame.lua l.46-82, l.662-700) — -- TWO DISTINCT KNOBS, and benilla ran them as one until 1494. The reference's split, which -- is now ours: -- -- B / F12 TOGGLEBACKPACK -> ToggleBackpack() — the BACKPACK's toggle. Closed: opens -- bag 0 ALONE. Already open: hides every container window there is. The -- asymmetry is the reference's own — one bag out, all bags in. -- SHIFT-B OPENALLBAGS -> OpenAllBags() — the ALL-bags toggle: everything open -- already closes the lot, anything else opens the lot. -- F8..F11 TOGGLEBAG1..4 -> ToggleBag(4..1) — one equipped bag each (note the -- reference's REVERSED numbering: TOGGLEBAG1 is bag 4). -- -- "All bags" = the backpack (bag 0, which always exists) plus each equipped-bag slot 1..4 -- that actually holds a bag (GetContainerNumSlots > 0); an empty slot has no window to -- show. The five windows, indexed by bag id (BENILLA_BAG_WINDOWS[bagId+1]) — one code path -- over all of them. The keyring is a seventh window with its own ToggleKeyRing: swept by -- the two close arms below (the ref's sweeps are over ALL ContainerFrames, which is what -- its keyring lives in), never counted as an open bag and never opened by them. BENILLA_BAG_WINDOWS = { "BenillaBagFrame", "BenillaBagFrame1", "BenillaBagFrame2", "BenillaBagFrame3", "BenillaBagFrame4" }
-- THE REFERENCE'S NAMES ARE THE REAL ENTRY POINTS, and our own UI calls THEM. -- -- This is how a 1.12 addon customises anything: it replaces a global and expects the -- client to call its replacement. `Bagnon_Core/core/Overrides.lua` is the canonical shape — -- local bToggleBackpack = ToggleBackpack -- ToggleBackpack = function() ... end -- and until now that override was INERT here, because the bag bindings and the bag button -- called `BenillaBagToggle_OnClick` directly and nothing ever looked up `ToggleBackpack`. -- Bagnon loaded, appeared in the AddOns list, replaced the globals, and the player still -- got the stock bags. The director saw that; no instrument here could, because the corpus -- survey loads addons and fires events but never CLICKS anything. -- -- The class is far wider than one addon: every "hook a global to change behaviour" addon is -- silently inert wherever our UI calls a benilla-named equivalent instead of the -- reference's name. `CloseAllBags`/`OpenBackpack`/`CloseBackpack` already lived under the -- ref's names in UiPanels.xml for exactly this reason; these are the three that did not. -- -- `OpenAllBags(forceOpen)` is the ref's SHIFT-B body (ContainerFrame.lua l.662-700) and it -- is a TOGGLE, not a plain open: one pass hides every open window while counting them -- against how many CAN be open, and if everything already was, that pass IS the close and -- it returns. `forceOpen` (the ref's own argument, used by callers that mean "open") skips -- the close arm. The open arm calls the GLOBALS `ToggleBackpack()`/`ToggleBag(1..4)` on a -- now-closed set — the ref's exact tail, so a bag addon holding either name gets both. function OpenAllBags(forceOpen) if UIParent and not UIParent:IsVisible() then return end local totalBags = 1 -- the backpack always counts for bagId = 1, 4 do if GetContainerNumSlots(bagId) > 0 then totalBags = totalBags + 1 end end local bagsOpen = 0 for _, name in ipairs(BENILLA_BAG_WINDOWS) do local frame = getglobal(name) if frame and frame:IsShown() then frame:Hide() bagsOpen = bagsOpen + 1 end end -- Swept with the rest, but never counted (ref: `if GetID() ~= KEYRING_CONTAINER`). local keyring = getglobal("BenillaKeyRingFrame") if keyring and keyring:IsShown() then keyring:Hide() end if bagsOpen >= totalBags and not forceOpen then return end ToggleBackpack() ToggleBag(1) ToggleBag(2) ToggleBag(3) ToggleBag(4) end
-- `ToggleBag(id)` — the ref's per-bag toggle (ContainerFrame.lua l.46-65), and the other -- global Bagnon replaces. Ours drives the same window the all-bags path does. -- -- The ref's `if size > 0` gate is load-bearing here and was missing until 1494: it is what -- keeps `OpenAllBags`' blind `ToggleBag(1..4)` tail from showing an empty slot's window. -- Bag 0 is exempt for the same reason `OpenBag` exempts it (it always exists even when the -- feed has not told us its size yet) — the ref gets that for free from its own always-16 -- backpack. function ToggleBag(id) id = id or 0 if id ~= 0 and GetContainerNumSlots(id) <= 0 then return end local frame = getglobal(BENILLA_BAG_WINDOWS[id + 1]) if not frame then return end if frame:IsShown() then frame:Hide() else BenillaBagWindow_Repaint(frame) frame:Show() end end
-- `OpenBag(id)` / `CloseBag(id)` / `IsBagOpen(id)` — ToggleBag's three siblings from the -- same reference file (ContainerFrame.lua l.144-185), and the last of that family that was -- still missing here. `Bagnon_Core/core/Overrides.lua` l.42/51 captures BOTH of the first -- two and calls the capture back for any bag Bagnon does not control — a nil call, on the -- ordinary path, for an addon that only *partly* takes the bags over. -- -- The reference's `OpenBag` opens a bag only when `GetContainerNumSlots(id) > 0`; ours keeps -- that gate for 1..4 and exempts bag 0, which always exists (the same rule `OpenAllBags` -- above already applies, for the same reason). function OpenBag(id) id = id or 0 if id ~= 0 and GetContainerNumSlots(id) <= 0 then return end local frame = getglobal(BENILLA_BAG_WINDOWS[id + 1]) if frame and not frame:IsShown() then BenillaBagWindow_Repaint(frame) frame:Show() end end
function CloseBag(id) local frame = getglobal(BENILLA_BAG_WINDOWS[(id or 0) + 1]) if frame and frame:IsShown() then frame:Hide() end end
-- ONE STATED DIVERGENCE. The reference returns the INDEX of the ContainerFrame showing that -- bag (1..NUM_CONTAINER_FRAMES) so its own code can `getglobal("ContainerFrame"..i)`; we -- ship no such pool (each bag has one fixed window), so there is no index to name and this -- answers 1 / nil. Every corpus caller — and the reference's own `ToggleBackpack` — uses it -- as a boolean; a caller that indexed the result would already be reaching for frames that -- do not exist here. function IsBagOpen(id) local frame = getglobal(BENILLA_BAG_WINDOWS[(id or 0) + 1]) if frame and frame:IsShown() then return 1 end return nil end
-- `ToggleBackpack()` — ref ContainerFrame.lua l.67-82, and NOT the all-bags toggle it was -- here until 1494: -- -- if ( IsBagOpen(0) ) then <hide every ContainerFrame> else ToggleBag(0) end -- -- Open arm: `ToggleBag(0)`, the backpack ALONE (through the global, so a bag addon holding -- `ToggleBag` gets it). -- ── The open-bag stack + layout law (ref ContainerFrame1.bags + -- updateContainerFrameAnchors, ContainerFrame.lua:472-552, transcribed shape) ───────────── -- Open windows stack bottom-right UPWARD in show order: the first at the bottom-right -- CLEARANCE CORNER, each next one anchored above the previous (TOPRIGHT → BOTTOMRIGHT, -- CONTAINER_SPACING=0 gap); when a stack would run off the top of the screen, the NEXT -- window starts a fresh column one CONTAINER_WIDTH further left. -- Out of scope (nothing here ever needs it): the ref's UI-scale/BankFrame-collision shrink -- branch (l.505-539) — benilla has no uiScale CVar and no bank window yet. -- -- The corner is `CONTAINER_OFFSET_X`/`CONTAINER_OFFSET_Y` — the two GLOBALS -- `UIParent_ManageFramePositions()` recomputes every time the bottom of the screen fills up -- or empties (UIParent.xml's var rows). Reading them live is the whole point and it is -- load-bearing, not tidiness: this file used to keep its own `local -- BENILLA_CONTAINER_OFFSET_X/Y = 0/70` shadow pair, which meant the stack sat at the -- no-bars-raised corner FOREVER — with a bottom multibar up, the lowest bag window drew -- straight through the bar's buttons (director-caught, decision 1499). A shadow copy of a -- managed value cannot be kept in sync by anyone; the fix is to have no copy. -- `BenillaBagStack_Relayout` is registered as a managed-position LISTENER at the end of this -- file, so a bar raised while bags are open re-seats them on the same pass that moves the -- cast bar and the chat frames. BENILLA_BAG_STACK = {} local BENILLA_CONTAINER_WIDTH = 192 local BENILLA_CONTAINER_SPACING = 0 local BENILLA_VISIBLE_CONTAINER_SPACING = 3

function BenillaBagStack_Relayout() -- Read the clearance corner FRESH on every pass — never cached in a local that outlives -- the call (see the law above). Decision 1499.) -- ── The item-push drop animation (decision 0887) ───────────────────────────────────────── -- An item lands in a bag: its icon pops in above the bag bar, hangs there, then falls into -- the button that took it and shrinks away. ref ItemAnim (MainMenuBarBagButtons.xml l.4-16 + -- .lua l.68-80, .lua l.92-94): each bag button owns a hidden child that, on ITEM_PUSH -- naming its own container, swaps in the pushed item's icon, rewinds to sequence time 0 and -- shows itself; OnAnimFinished hides it again. A second push on the same button RESTARTS it -- (SetSequenceTime(0,0)); pushes into different bags run independently. That is exactly the -- machine below, with the reference's ITEM_PUSH `arg1` translated from its inventory-slot -- vocabulary (20..23) into ours (bagId 1..4) app-side — ui_loot.rs `push_container` carries -- the byte-verified selector. -- -- The reference's is a <Model> playing Interface\ItemAnimations\ForcedBackpackItem.mdx — a -- single 4-vertex quad on one animated bone, i.e. a 2D icon card with keyframed scale, alpha -- and offset. benilla has no Model widget (decision 0137's Cooldown took the same posture: -- model the mechanism, let our own renderer draw it), so it is a Texture driven by the -- model's OWN tracks, read out of the shipped .m2 with `benilla-extract m2anim`/`m2bones`: -- -- sequence 0, CLAMP (plays once), duration 1.000 s -- texture-weight (alpha) 0.000→0.0 0.133→1.0 0.267→1.0 1.000→0.0 linear -- bone 0 scale 0.000→1.0 0.133→1.2 0.267→1.0 1.000→0.014 linear -- bone 0 translation 0.000→(0,0) 0.500→(0,0) 1.000→(+0.010,-0.040) -- the quad itself: 0.03 x 0.03 model units, blend Alpha, unlit, no depth write -- -- So: fade in over the first 133 ms while swelling to 1.2x; settle back to full size by -- 267 ms; from there dwindle and fade continuously for the remaining 733 ms — while the -- POSITION holds until the half-second and only then falls. The three tracks deliberately -- do not share a schedule: the card is already down to ~0.69 size and ~0.68 alpha when it -- starts moving, so the drop reads as the icon being drawn into the bag rather than as a -- solid tile sliding. Those numbers are the file's, not ours. -- -- THE MODEL-UNIT → PIXEL SCALE is no longer ours to calibrate: the <Model> widget's -- projection is RE-recorded now (wow-re `system/ui/scratch/modelframe-animation-clock.md`, -- dispatched over the pet bar's B228 and folded back with it). The ortho leg gives -- -- px per model unit = (5/3) * modelScale * layoutScale * screenHeightPx -- -- which in FrameXML units is **1280 * modelScale * layoutScale**, aspect- and -- resolution-independent, with the model ORIGIN at the frame rect's bottom-left. The ref's -- `ItemAnimTemplate` (MainMenuBarBagButtons.xml:4) carries **no `scale` attribute**, so -- modelScale is 1 and the constant is a flat 1280. Decision 0887's named gap is closed. -- -- This REPLACES a back-fit, and the back-fit is worth naming because it looked like -- evidence. The old 1200 came from assuming CooldownFrameTemplate's 0.04-unit sweep -- *exactly* covers a 36 px action button at its scale="0.75" (⇒ K = 1200). The assumption -- is the error: at the real projection that sweep is 0.04 · 1280 · 0.75 = **38.4 px**, so -- it overhangs its button by 6.7% rather than fitting it — exactly as the autocast shine's -- 30.72 px square overhangs its 30 px button. Solving against a wrong premise produced a -- number that then "cross-checked" against a second model derived the same wrong way, and -- both files cited the agreement as the reason to trust it. -- -- Everything below is the model's own ratios times this constant, so the correction lands -- in one place and the animation stays in proportion. BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_PX_PER_UNIT = 1280 BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_DURATION = 1.0
-- ── The widget rect, and why the card is not placed against the button ───────────────── -- A `<Model>` with no `<Size>` and no `setAllPoints` takes its rect from the **M2 header -- bounding box** (`MD20+0xB4`, max−min per axis), consumed RAW as layout units — unlike -- CSimpleTexture's texel fallback, there is no AbsDimension conversion. So the ref's -- ItemAnim widget is **42.41 x 124.72**, nothing like the 36-square everyone assumes from -- looking at the XML, and **model-space (0,0,0) lands on that rect's BOTTOM-LEFT corner**. -- (wow-re `system/ui/scratch/modelframe-implicit-size-law.md`, §5-cross-checked: vtable -- 0x81c5d8 +0x1c/+0x20 -> 0x76d080/0x76d0d0, bbox source 0x713640 at `713661 add esi,0xb4`. -- The one worker who read `MD20+0xD0` — the VertexBox — got an all-zero box and concluded -- the widget was degenerate; that wrong premise is exactly what the pair round exists to -- catch, and it is why this looked unresolvable in 0887.) -- -- That rect is the whole reason this animation reads the way it does: it stands 124.72 tall -- off the button's own bottom edge, so the card's travel band reaches **54 px above the -- button's top**. Decision 0887 could not know that and placed the card against the -- button's CENTER instead, which is what put it in the wrong place in x and gave it no -- horizontal drift at all. BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_FRAME_W = 42.41 BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_FRAME_H = 124.72 -- Where that rect hangs off the button: the ref anchors the widget's BOTTOMRIGHT to the -- button's, 10 in from the right for the five bag buttons and flush (0) for the keyring — -- MainMenuBarBagButtons.xml l.19-27 (BagSlotButtonTemplate) and l.152-160 (KeyRingButton). -- Per-button, so it is an OnLoad argument, not a constant. BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_ANCHOR_X = -10
-- ── The model's own numbers, unrounded ──────────────────────────────────────────────── -- Every one of these was rounded in 0887 and every rounding moved the card. The quad span -- read as 0.03 (it is 0.0288 — a 4% size error), and the translation as (0.010, -0.040) -- (which alone accounts for half a pixel of the landing point). -- -- The bone transform is `v' = pivot + T(t) + S(t) * (v - pivot)` — three wow-re workers -- derived that independently in three matrix conventions and agreed. The pivot -- (M2CompBone+0x60) is NOT the quad's centre: it sits 0.23 px right and 0.07 px above it, -- so the card shrinks *almost* in place and drifts a fifth of a pixel doing it. Keeping -- the pivot as its own term rather than folding it into the centre is what makes this -- reproduce the reference exactly at all three sampled times instead of nearly. -- Bone 0's ROTATION track is empty (nKeys = 0), so there is no roll to model. BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_PIVOT_X = 0.017580900341272354 BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_PIVOT_Y = 0.053958501666784286 BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_QUAD_X = 0.017400000942870975 BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_QUAD_Y = 0.053900001570582390 BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_QUAD_SPAN = 0.028800001833587885
-- {time, value} keyframes, linear between (M2 track interpolation 1) — the file's own keys, -- at full precision. The three tracks keep DIFFERENT schedules and that is the whole feel: -- the card fades up while swelling to 1.2x over 133 ms, settles back to full size at -- 267 ms, then dwindles and fades *continuously* for the remaining 733 ms — while its -- position holds until the half second and only then falls. So it is already at ~0.69 size -- and ~0.68 alpha when it starts to move, and it is invisible by the time it lands. BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_ALPHA = { {0.000, 0.0}, {0.133, 1.0}, {0.267, 1.0}, {1.000, 0.0} } BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_SCALE = { {0.000, 1.0}, {0.133, 1.2000000476837158}, {0.267, 1.0}, {1.000, 0.01441549975425005} } -- Translation is per-AXIS: the card falls 51.4 px and drifts 13.3 px RIGHT, so one shared -- 0..1 "drop" curve (0887's shape) cannot express it — the old code had no horizontal term -- at all and moved the card the wrong way in x when it inferred one. BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_TRANS_X = { {0.000, 0.0}, {0.500, 0.0}, {1.000, 0.010394600220024586} } BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_TRANS_Y = { {0.000, 0.0}, {0.500, 0.0}, {1.000, -0.040167398750782013} }
-- Sample a {time, value} keyframe list at `t`, linear between keys, clamped at both ends -- (the M2 sampler's own shape for a CLAMP sequence). function BenillaItemPushAnim_Sample(track, t) local last = table.getn(track) if t <= track[1][1] then return track[1][2] end for i = 2, last do local key = track[i] if t <= key[1] then local prev = track[i - 1] local span = key[1] - prev[1] if span <= 0 then return key[2] end return prev[2] + (key[2] - prev[2]) * (t - prev[1]) / span end end return track[last][2] end
-- Place/size/fade the card for the current clock, from the model's own transform. -- -- The card's centre in MODEL space is `pivot + T(t) + S(t)*(quadCentre - pivot)`; times the -- projection constant that is its offset in layout units from the model origin, which is -- the widget rect's bottom-left corner. The rect's own BOTTOMRIGHT hangs off the button's, -- so the card is placed against the BUTTON'S BOTTOMRIGHT — never its centre — and the -- frame width is what converts between the two. -- -- On screen: a button-sized card appears with its bottom edge ~13.6 px ABOVE the button's -- top, pops to 1.2x and back while fading in, hangs there through the first half second, -- then falls down-and-right INTO the button, shrinking to a half-pixel point at its centre -- as it fades out. Reproduces the reference at t = 0, 0.133 and 1.0 to the hundredth of a -- pixel (`modelframe-implicit-size-law.md` §3's table). -- -- NOT modelled, deliberately, and both are named in the record: the reference's widget -- CLIPS the card to its own rect, which shaves 1.94 px off the right edge at the 1.2x peak -- **at 4:3 only** (16:10 and 16:9 clear it); and the widget clears the depth buffer inside -- that 124.72-tall rect every paint. benilla draws this as a Texture, not a Model, so it -- inherits neither — reproducing an aspect-conditional sliver would be hard-coding a -- rendering artefact rather than modelling the mechanism that causes it. function BenillaItemPushAnim_Paint(anim) local t = anim.elapsed local k = BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_PX_PER_UNIT local scale = BenillaItemPushAnim_Sample(BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_SCALE, t) local size = BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_QUAD_SPAN * scale * k local cx = (BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_PIVOT_X + BenillaItemPushAnim_Sample(BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_TRANS_X, t) + scale * (BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_QUAD_X - BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_PIVOT_X)) * k local cy = (BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_PIVOT_Y + BenillaItemPushAnim_Sample(BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_TRANS_Y, t) + scale * (BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_QUAD_Y - BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_PIVOT_Y)) * k anim:SetWidth(size) anim:SetHeight(size) anim:SetPoint("CENTER", anim:GetParent(), "BOTTOMRIGHT", anim.anchorX - BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_FRAME_W + cx, cy) anim:SetAlpha(BenillaItemPushAnim_Sample(BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_ALPHA, t)) end
-- ref ItemAnim_OnLoad (l.68-70): the card listens for ITEM_PUSH and nothing else. It is -- authored hidden, so it costs no OnUpdate until a push shows it (events reach hidden -- frames; OnUpdate does not — the reference's own split). function BenillaItemPushAnim_OnLoad(anim, containerId, anchorX) anim.containerId = containerId -- The widget's own offset from the button's BOTTOMRIGHT: -10 for the five bag buttons, -- flush 0 for the keyring (the ref's two different anchors — see the constant block). anim.anchorX = anchorX or BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_ANCHOR_X anim.icon = getglobal(anim:GetName() .. "Icon") anim.elapsed = 0 anim:RegisterEvent("ITEM_PUSH") end
-- ref ItemAnim_OnEvent (l.72-80): `if this:GetParent():GetID() == arg1`, then -- ReplaceIconTexture(arg2) / SetSequence(0) / SetSequenceTime(0,0) / Show. A push into a bag -- with no button (a bank bag) matches nothing and animates nowhere, there and here. function BenillaItemPushAnim_OnEvent(anim) if arg1 ~= anim.containerId then return end anim.icon:SetTexture(arg2) anim.elapsed = 0 -- Seat the card above its button rather than at load: the bag bar's own level is set in -- the BUTTON's OnLoad (BenillaActionBarArt_SeatAbove), which the loader may run after -- this child exists. Re-deriving it per push is one call and can never read it stale. anim:SetFrameLevel(anim:GetParent():GetFrameLevel() + 1) BenillaItemPushAnim_Paint(anim) anim:Show() end
-- The CLAMP sequence's end is the ref's OnAnimFinished → this:Hide() (l.92-94). function BenillaItemPushAnim_OnUpdate(anim, elapsed) anim.elapsed = anim.elapsed + (elapsed or 0) if anim.elapsed >= BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_DURATION then anim:Hide() return end BenillaItemPushAnim_Paint(anim) end
-- The bag BAR's five buttons (the backpack toggle + the four equipped-bag slots) — the row -- Disable_/Enable_BagButtons greys as a unit. Distinct from UiPanels.xml's BAG_WINDOWS, -- which is the five bag *windows* those buttons open. BENILLA_BAG_BUTTONS = { "MainMenuBarBackpackButton", "CharacterBag0Slot", "CharacterBag1Slot", "CharacterBag2Slot", "CharacterBag3Slot" }
-- Disable_BagButtons / Enable_BagButtons — ref MainMenuBarBagButtons.lua l.102-128, called -- by GameMenuFrame's OnShow/OnHide (decision 0674) and by nothing else: while the game menu -- holds the screen, the whole bag row greys out. That is the *visible* half of a rule the -- panel manager already enforces (ShowUIPanel's native-center gate refuses every window -- while the menu is up — UiPanels.xml `CanOpenPanels`); without it the bags would look -- clickable and simply do nothing. -- -- Mapping onto benilla's row: the ref's MainMenuBarBackpackButton is MainMenuBarBackpackButton and -- CharacterBag0..3Slot are CharacterBag0Slot..4 — and in BOTH cases the greying goes onto -- the button's `$parentIcon` LAYER texture, never onto a state texture. That is the -- reference's own structure and it is load-bearing here: a disabled button draws its -- DisabledTexture, and with none set it draws no state texture at all -- (`ButtonState::region_visible`), so greying a NormalTexture would grey something already -- gone. The four slots' UI-Quickslot2 rings ARE state textures and do vanish while -- disabled unless the slot states one explicitly — so what you should see is the -- ring stay put and the bag icon grey — which is why each slot repeats its ring as -- DisabledTexture (see the slot instances below). function Disable_BagButtons() for _, button in ipairs(BENILLA_BAG_BUTTONS) do local b = getglobal(button) b:Disable() SetDesaturation(b.icon, 1) end end
function Enable_BagButtons() for _, button in ipairs(BENILLA_BAG_BUTTONS) do local b = getglobal(button) b:Enable() SetDesaturation(b.icon, nil) end -- The four slots' own paint decides their restored colour: an item locked on the cursor -- wants its 0.4 grey back, which the un-desaturate above does not restore (it clears -- the greyscale flag, not the tint). for i = 1, 4 do BenillaBagBarSlot_Update(getglobal("CharacterBag" .. (i - 1) .. "Slot")) end end

Scripts.OnLoad: self.icon = getglobal("MainMenuBarBackpackButtonIconTexture") if BenillaActionBarArt_SeatAbove then BenillaActionBarArt_SeatAbove(self) end
